clue.text: See 16
Lacking branches, trees round British Libray start to sway

indicators.note: the trees go round the library's initials, holding them inside

parts.note: limes are lime trees, a common street tree
BL is the abbreviation for the British Library (the clue misprints Library)

indicators.note: start to sway asks for the opening letter of that word

explanation.surface: Trees with their branches lopped stand around the British Library, beginning to sway.
explanation.walkthrough: BL is the British Library (printed with a typo, 'Libray'); 'round' and 'start to' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree without branches is literally without limbs, so the word fits the cut-back trees.

clue.text: Healthy finance keeps Oscar adequately provided for

parts.note: being well means being in good health

indicators.note: the funding word holds the letter inside it, as a keeper does

parts.note: to fund something is to finance it
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Healthy funding keeps the Oscar-winning film properly resourced.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-found ship or house is fully equipped, i.e. properly supplied with everything needed.

clue.text: Finally deal with German state?

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of deal

parts.note: and means together with, so with gives this joining word

explanation.surface: A question of whether we should at last strike an agreement with Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: a German federal state is called a Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany's federal states, such as Bavaria, are officially called Länder, singular Land.

clue.text: Sat around finally after work suggested

indicators.note: the sitting word goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat gives posed

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of after

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone sat about and, at last, came up with a suggestion after finishing their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' is the verb pose (for a portrait); 'around' encloses, and 'finally' takes the end of 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proposed and suggested are synonyms: both mean put forward an idea for consideration.

clue.text: Standing up Irish athlete is more dangerous

indicators.note: in a down entry standing up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a skier is a winter-sports athlete

explanation.surface: An Irish athlete who rises to their feet runs a greater hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing up' turns IR into RI, a reversal convention for down clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskier is the comparative of risky, and risky means dangerous, so the two comparatives match.

clue.text: Pale-coloured mutant deer blow up

indicators.note: a mutant is changed in form, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A sci-fi scene: a pale mutant deer explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutant' rearranges DEERBLOWUP.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft light shade of blue, so it describes a pale colour; here it works adjectivally.

clue.text: Extra thin

definitions.meaning: a ... item is an additional one kept in reserve
a ... figure is lean, with no excess flesh

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both surplus to need and lean or meagre in build.

clue.text: Ramsay's gutted — recipe comes out scarcely sweet

indicators.note: the plate of food comes out around the chef's letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a dish is a prepared recipe on the plate

indicators.note: a gutted word loses its insides, leaving only the outer letters of the chef's name

explanation.surface: Gordon Ramsay is gutted when a recipe turns out barely sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Ramsay is a famous British TV chef; 'gutted' keeps only his name's ends, and 'comes out' has the dish around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means somewhat, so a slightly dry wine is only a little short of sweetness.

clue.text: Life-forms are aeroplanes, nothing less

indicators.note: less means minus, so the zero letter is taken away

parts.note: Boeings are aeroplanes made by the US manufacturer
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A claim that airliners are living things, with nothing missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O (nothing) from BOEINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beings are living creatures, the entities a biologist would call organisms.

clue.text: Feigns sickness finding fish drug in chocolate bar

indicators.note: in places the fish and drug inside the chocolate bar

parts.note: a Mars is a well-known chocolate bar
ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to be ill after finding fish and drugs in their chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; E for ecstasy is standard crossword slang. Mars is a British chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend illness to avoid work, so it is to fake being sick.

clue.text: European cautious about getting tired

indicators.note: the cautious word goes about the European letter

parts.note: wary means cautious, on guard

explanation.surface: A careful European grows exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside WARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Weary is a straightforward synonym for tired or fatigued.

clue.text: Existence of metals

parts.note: the word supplies two metals: LI is the chemical symbol for lithium and FE for iron
the word supplies two metals: LI is the chemical symbol for lithium and FE for iron

explanation.surface: A question about how metals exist.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'metals' supplies both pieces: lithium's symbol Li and iron's symbol Fe, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Life and existence are synonyms for the state of being alive.

clue.text: Weaving silk unseen makes a difference

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Weaving silk in a way no one sees produces a distinctive result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaving' rearranges SILKUNSEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlikeness is dissimilarity, the state of things not being alike.

clue.text: Party supporter is ingenuous standing up to be sick

indicators.note: in a down entry standing up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a fan is a supporter, as of a team
naif means naive or ingenuous
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: A supporter admits he is naive enough to stand up and be sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns FANNAIF into FIANNAF. Fianna Fáil is one of Ireland's main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major Irish political party, so it is an example of a party.

clue.text: Examines the way university shuts down

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a machine that dies stops working, shuts down

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises how a university closes.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something is to examine it closely, so both verbs mean scrutinise.

clue.text: Dress right to speak about mean poet

parts.note: a robe is a dress or gown

indicators.note: the speaking word goes about the mean one, enclosing it

parts.note: to tell is to speak or say
low means mean or base, as in a low trick

explanation.surface: An instruction to dress properly and talk about a stingy poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The puzzle honours this American poet: Land of Unlikeness, Lord Weary's Castle, Life Studies, Imitations and The Old Glory, his books, are spread through the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a major twentieth-century American confessional writer of verse, so he is an example of the category.

clue.text: Matador is eccentric broadcaster

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bullfighter is an oddball who talks on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges MATADORIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure carrying aerials sends out signals, so it literally broadcasts programmes.

clue.text: Change round, almost insulting woman

indicators.note: the coins go round the shortened word, enclosing it

parts.note: pence are coins, loose change

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rude means insulting

explanation.surface: Someone turns around and is nearly rude to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' is loose coins, not a verb; 'almost' drops a final letter and 'round' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is a woman's first name, so the clue defines it by category.

clue.text: Poetry about new eastern city

indicators.note: the poems go about the new letter, enclosing it

parts.note: odes are poems, so poetry gives this plural

explanation.surface: Fresh verse about the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside ODES, then E follows. Odense is Denmark's third city.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is a Danish city on the island of Funen, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen.

clue.text: Online winner one to get rid of

parts.note: E as in e-mail stands for electronic, online
a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: An internet champion is someone to oust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one to get rid of' reads as someone to be removed, but defines the person doing the removing.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is a person who expels tenants, i.e. gets rid of them.

clue.text: Clean city out

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
under means unconscious, out cold

explanation.surface: A clean-up campaign to get rid of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash them, to make them clean.

clue.text: Extended recliner without the third part

indicators.note: the third letter of the reclining chair is removed

parts.note: a lounger is a reclining chair

explanation.surface: A reclining chair stretched out, minus its third section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without the third part' drops U, the third letter of LOUNGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Longer means extended in length, made to stretch further.

clue.text: Fearsome female artist seen in European port

indicators.note: seen in means the artist's letters appear inside the port

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A formidable woman painter spotted in a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword artist; 'seen in' is the container signal and Vigo is in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, bad-tempered woman, so a fearsome female fits.

clue.text: Restrictions left out copies

indicators.note: out means taken away, so the letter for left is removed

parts.note: limitations are restrictions

explanation.surface: Restrictions are lifted from copied goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from LIMITATIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitations are copies or fakes of an original.

clue.text: Chalmie had been first and did nothing

parts.note: Chalmie is the setter, who refers to themself as I
D as in I'd is short for had
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: The setter claims to have been in front and to have done nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for I, the setter writing in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Idled means passed time doing nothing useful, loafed.

clue.text: Knowledge finally lost by deceased ruler

indicators.note: finally lost means the last letter goes

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
D is short for dead, deceased

explanation.surface: A deceased ruler's knowledge has finally been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally lost' drops E from LORE; D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is a ruler or master, as in feudal lord.

clue.text: Holiday company's American decline begins

indicators.note: begins says the declining word comes first, before the American letter

parts.note: to sag is to droop, to decline

explanation.surface: A holiday firm's American business starts to slump.
explanation.walkthrough: Saga is a British travel company specialising in holidays for over-50s.
explanation.definitionFit: Saga is a UK firm selling package holidays, so it is a holiday company by name.

clue.text: Capital loans maintain Scottish town

indicators.note: maintain means hold, so the phrase holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Money lent from the capital keeps a Scottish town going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintain' signals letters held across 'capitAL LOAns'. Alloa is a town in central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town on the Forth, in Clackmannanshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Articles about shrew get popular, on the other hand

indicators.note: the two articles go about the nagging word

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles
a shrew is a nagging woman, a nag
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces about a scold become popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' gives two words, the and a; 'about' sends them round the shrew, and 'get' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a contrasting point, just as the idiom 'on the other hand' does.

clue.text: Familiar parrot swallows German flag

indicators.note: the pair of words swallow the German letter between them

parts.note: old means familiar, as in an old story
a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A familiar parrot gulps down a German flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' takes in G between the two words. A lory is an Australasian parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is the nickname of the flag of the United States.

clue.text: Building legal action to restrain Returning Officer

indicators.note: the legal action holds the officer letters inside it

parts.note: a case is a legal action

indicators.note: returning means the officer's letters are read backwards

parts.note: LT is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A legal case brought to curb an election's returning officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning Officer' looks like the UK election official; it is a reversal indicator plus Lt, lieutenant. 'to restrain' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a large fortified building.
